title: RC charge or discharge after a voltage step
description: Calculate a capacitor's arbitrary-initial-condition step trajectory, relative-error settling time, stored energy, and accumulated resistor pulse energy.
formula: tau=RC; vC=Vs+(V0-Vs)exp(-t/tau); iC=(Vs-vC)/R; t_settle=-tau ln(epsilon); EC=C vC^2/2; ER=C(Vs-V0)^2[1-exp(-2t/tau)]/2
assumptions: Ideal constant capacitance and positive series resistance driven by an ideal constant voltage after t=0; R includes source resistance and capacitor ESR where their lumped approximation is valid.
Positive current flows from source into capacitor. Vs=0 describes discharge; no separate inverse calculator is counted.

Settling tolerance is a fraction of the initial-to-final voltage difference, not an ADC or digital threshold specification. For V0=Vs there is no transient and the reported normalized settling time is a conventional time-scale metric only.
Stored energy excludes dielectric loss; resistor pulse energy does not establish a resistor pulse-rating or safety certification.

Voltage increments and accumulated resistive energy use expm1 so arbitrarily short positive elapsed times do not lose the exponential difference to subtraction; adding a tiny increment to a nonzero initial voltage remains subject to ordinary floating-point resolution.

title: Unbuffered two-stage RC ladder startup
description: Compute both capacitor-node voltages and the downstream capacitor current in a passive two-stage RC ladder, retaining interstage loading instead of multiplying independent RC step responses.
formula: a=R1R2C1C2; b=R1C1+R1C2+R2C2; tau_s=(b+sqrt(b^2-4a))/2; tau_f=a/tau_s; v2=Vs[1-(tau_s exp(-t/tau_s)-tau_f exp(-t/tau_f))/(tau_s-tau_f)]; v1=v2+R2 C2 dv2/dt
assumptions: Topology: ideal source, R1, node one, R2, node two in sequence; C1 and C2 connect their respective nodes to common ground. Both capacitors initially uncharged; no external output load or buffer.
All four components are positive and linear. R1 incorporates source resistance; parasitic inductance, capacitor ESR and leakage are neglected.
The R1C2 cross term explicitly accounts for downstream loading. This is a startup transient calculation, not cutoff or filter synthesis.

The relative discriminant must be at least 1e-8 for distinct-pole numerical conditioning. The fast time constant is evaluated as a/tau_s to avoid subtracting nearly equal b and sqrt(discriminant). The shared Rust step_overdamped_scaled(t,1/tau_s,1/tau_f,Vs) primitive evaluates the same analytic two-real-pole step with stable short-time conditioning and amplitude-aware scaling to preserve representable voltages when the normalized response underflows; no additional time exclusion or seed output is used.

title: Underdamped series-RLC step ringing and peak stress
description: Predict capacitor voltage, series current, first voltage overshoot and a conservative error-envelope settling bound following a source step in an initially unenergized series RLC circuit.
formula: alpha=R/(2L); wn=1/sqrt(LC); zeta=alpha/wn; wd=sqrt(wn^2-alpha^2); vC=Vs{1-exp(-alpha t)[cos(wd t)+(alpha/wd)sin(wd t)]}; i=Vs exp(-alpha t)sin(wd t)/(L wd); tp=pi/wd; Mp=exp(-alpha pi/wd)
assumptions: Series RLC with output across C, zero initial capacitor voltage and zero initial inductor current; positive source step.
Linear unsaturated L and linear C; R is total series resistance including source resistance, winding resistance and ESR where the series lumped model holds.
Only the underdamped domain is implemented: (R/(2L))^2 must be at most (1-1e-8)/(LC). Critical and overdamped responses are not approximated by this expression.

Settling output is a sufficient envelope bound, not the exact last threshold crossing: absolute normalized voltage error <= exp(-alpha t)/sqrt(1-zeta^2). No AC resonance, Q or filter synthesis outputs are counted.
Distributed parasitics, nonlinear clamps and component pulse/voltage ratings require separate checks.

The shared Rust step_underdamped_scaled(omega_n*time,damping_ratio,v_step) primitive evaluates the same analytic step with stable short-time conditioning and amplitude-aware scaling to preserve representable voltages when the normalized response underflows. Its first argument is dimensionless natural-frequency time, not damped-frequency time or elapsed seconds; no additional short-time exclusion or user-facing seed output is introduced.

title: Periodic RC charging extrema under two-level excitation
description: Find periodic steady-state capacitor extrema and ripple for alternating source levels with arbitrary high and low durations, including incomplete charging memory between pulses.
formula: a=exp(-Th/RC); b=exp(-Tl/RC); Vmin=[Vl(1-b)+b Vh(1-a)]/(1-ab); Vmax=Vmin+(Vh-Vmin)(1-a); Vavg=(VhTh+VlTl)/(Th+Tl)
assumptions: An ideal voltage source switches between Vhigh and Vlow through one unchanged positive R into one linear capacitor; no DC load.
Periodic steady state is assumed, not the first pulse after startup. Vhigh>=Vlow defines extrema; source levels can be signed.
No frequency-domain filter synthesis, digital threshold, transistor switching loss or converter sizing is included.

Both pulse durations divided by RC must be at least 1e-7, retaining the researched conservative numerical domain. Exponential differences use expm1; ripple and edge currents are evaluated directly from the source-level difference rather than subtracting rounded absolute capacitor voltages.

title: RL current buildup or decay after a voltage step
description: Predict inductor current, inductor voltage and fractional settling time for a closed series RL circuit with an arbitrary initial current.
formula: tau=L/R; If=Vs/R; iL=If+(I0-If)exp(-t/tau); vL=(Vs-RI0)exp(-t/tau); t_settle=-tau ln(epsilon)
assumptions: Linear, unsaturated inductor with constant L; positive R includes winding and source resistance.
An actual closed RL path remains after switching; an opened inductor, avalanche event or diode clamp is not represented by this model.
Current is oriented from source through R and L; vL uses the passive sign convention.
Settling is normalized to the initial-to-final current difference; when I0=If it is only a time-scale metric. Magnetic stored energy is owned by the magnetics lane.

Initial-current decay and driven buildup are evaluated separately with exp and expm1, retaining source-free residual decay and very short-time buildup without subtraction of nearly equal exponentials.

title: Constant-current capacitor ramp and energy
description: Calculate the voltage and stored-energy change of a capacitor subjected to a constant signed current, without selecting an active current-source circuit.
formula: dv/dt=I/C; vC=V0+It/C; deltaQ=It; EC=C vC^2/2; deltaE=C(vC^2-V0^2)/2
assumptions: Ideal current excitation of a passive, linear capacitor; current-source compliance, load and leakage must be checked externally.
Positive current enters the positive voltage terminal; a negative current describes discharge and may cross zero voltage mathematically.
This is not op-amp slew-rate design or switch-mode converter sizing. Polarized capacitor voltage limits are not modeled.
No ESR voltage step, ESL, dielectric absorption or voltage-dependent capacitance is included.
Energy change uses deltaQ*(V0+deltaQ/(2C)), algebraically identical to the difference of squared voltages, to avoid subtracting rounded stored energies for a small charge increment.

title: Two-capacitor charge redistribution through resistance
description: Predict common final voltage, redistribution current, individual capacitor trajectories, transferred charge, and irreversible energy loss when two initially charged capacitors are connected through resistance.
formula: Ceq=C1C2/(C1+C2); tau=R Ceq; Vf=(C1V1+C2V2)/(C1+C2); deltaV(t)=(V1-V2)exp(-t/tau); Eloss=Ceq(V1-V2)^2/2
assumptions: Capacitors share a common negative reference and their positive terminals are joined through positive R; no external source or load remains connected.
C1 and C2 are linear; R includes switch resistance and ESR, with parasitic inductance negligible on the redistribution time scale.
Zero resistance is excluded: the ideal zero-R two-capacitor paradox is outside this dissipative model.

The general unequal-capacitance result is derived from charge conservation and the capacitor energy law; the cited Berkeley example presents equal-capacitance and voltage-source limits. No switched-capacitor converter or MOSFET bootstrap sizing is performed.

Transferred charge and accumulated loss use expm1 for short-time exponential differences. Individual node voltages combine initial-state exponential decay with equilibrium-voltage buildup, preserving t=0 continuity and small residuals when equilibrium is zero; adding a tiny increment to a nonzero absolute voltage remains subject to machine resolution.

title: RC tracking of a finite-slope voltage ramp
description: Predict capacitor voltage, charging current and tracking lag when the source voltage changes linearly rather than instantaneously.
formula: Vs(t)=Vs0+mt; tau=RC; vC=Vs0+m(t-tau)+(V0-Vs0+m tau)exp(-t/tau); iC=Cm+(Vs0-V0-m tau)exp(-t/tau)/R
assumptions: A linear capacitor is driven through constant positive R by an ideal voltage source whose specified ramp persists throughout the selected elapsed time.
Source-ramp slope is not imposed capacitor current: current starts according to initial conditions and approaches C times the ramp slope.
Supports signed slopes and arbitrary initial capacitor voltage; no limiter or piecewise ramp-end response is modeled.

This is time-domain startup tracking, not op-amp slew-rate or frequency-domain filter design. The shared Rust expm1mx_ratio(x) primitive evaluates (exp(x)-1-x)/x^2 accurately near zero, with analytic value 0.5 at zero. The ramp term is slope*time*(time/tau)*expm1mx_ratio(-time/tau), avoiding premature underflow of the unscaled quadratic remainder without new time exclusions. Initial-state and source terms use separately conditioned exp/expm1 factors; adding a tiny contribution to a nonzero absolute voltage remains subject to machine resolution.
